When you rebase a branch, Git rewrites the commit history and changes the commit hashes. Because the local and remote histories no longer match, Git will reject a standard `git push` to prevent overwriting history.

If your local rebased branch is the version you want, you need to force-push it to the remote.

### Recommended Solution
Use the `--force-with-lease` flag. This is safer than a standard `--force` push because it ensures you won't accidentally overwrite any remote commits that you haven't fetched yet:

```bash
git push origin <branch-name> --force-with-lease
```
